Done. All tests pass and `go vet` is clean.

## What I implemented

`book_store.go` now computes the minimum basket cost for the Book Store discount problem from `.docs/instructions.md`.

**Approach:** Count copies per title (5 titles), then run an exact dynamic program over the sorted per-title counts. Because all titles are symmetric, the canonical state is just the counts sorted descending. From each state it tries every valid group size (1–5) and every choice of which titles to take one copy from, memoizing results.

**Why not the obvious greedy?** The naive "always take the largest group from the most-copied titles" strategy is provably suboptimal here — e.g. the 22-book case (`6,6,6,2,2` copies) expects **14560** (four groups of 4 + two of 3), but the greedy gives 14640 (two groups of 5 + four of 3). The DP explores the grouping space exactly, so it finds the true minimum in every case.

**One bug I hit and fixed:** my first version let the bitmask select exhausted (zero-copy) titles, driving counts negative and overflowing the stack. Since counts are sorted descending, only the first `k` positions have copies left, so I restricted the mask to those positions.

I did not touch `book_store_test.go` or `cases_test.go`, and created no new files.
